:::{#exm-conjugate-transpose}
#### The conjugate transpose of a $2 \times 3$ matrix

For

$$
\underbrace{\matr{A}}_{2 \times 3} =
\begin{bmatrix}
1 + i & 2 & 0 \\
-i & 3 - 2\,i & 4
\end{bmatrix},
$$

transposing gives a $3 \times 2$ matrix,
and conjugating each of its entries gives

$$
\underbrace{\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}}}_{3 \times 2} =
\begin{bmatrix}
1 - i & i \\
2 & 3 + 2\,i \\
0 & 4
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

For instance, $(\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}})_{12} = \overline{a_{21}} = \overline{-i} = i$.
The transpose alone would have $-i$ in that position,
so for a matrix with an entry that is not real, $\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}}$ and $\tp{\matr{A}}$ differ.
For a real matrix, conjugating changes nothing, so $\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}} = \tp{\matr{A}}$.

:::
